subject: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the LocoProp evaluation for trust-theory. The pitch: second-order optimizers give state-of-the-art training quality but their memory footprint and compute cost keep them off our budget-constrained runs. Our LocoProp release (AISTATS'22) constructs layerwise local losses — per-neuron targets set in the backward pass, then independent parallel updates per layer — and gets close to second-order performance using only first-order optimizers.

If that holds on our workloads, it's a direct GPU-hours reduction across the portfolio's recurring training jobs.

Milestones:
- May 8: benchmark reproduction (squared loss + layerwise Bregman divergence variants).
- Jun 12: head-to-head on two internal trust-model training jobs — wall-clock, memory, final eval quality.
- Jul 10: adopt/pass recommendation.

Bruno owns staffing. Giannis is tech lead.

Ximena
